sections.title: Every proportion: report + name the group

blocks.text: Report as a percentage to **1 decimal place** and name the reference group: **40.0% of commuters**. The course outline says answers without the group lose one point. (S1 reporting rule)

sections.title: Worked table example: let the reference group set the denominator

blocks.text: Example counts: among 25 commuters, 10 cycle and 15 do not; among 15 noncommuters, 5 cycle and 10 do not. Total = 40. (Notes sections 1-2; practice Q1)

blocks.setup: One table: commuters: 10 cycle, 15 do not (25 total); noncommuters: 5 cycle, 10 do not (15 total). Choose the reference group named in the question.

steps.label: Column: commuters among cyclists
steps.text: 10 / 15 = **66.7% of cyclists**. For the earlier column-denominator error, use the cycle-column total 15, not the commuter-row total 25.

blocks.takeaway: The shared count is 10; the percentage changes because the reference group changes.

blocks.text: Conditional probability assumes equally weighted cases and a nonempty reference group. (Notes section 1.4)

blocks.setup: For a mean score by course section, each nonempty section becomes one output row.

steps.label: Rows returned
steps.text: One row per nonempty group. Four nonempty sections = **4 rows**, even if the original data had 120 students. (Notes section 3.2; 2025 past paper Q3)

steps.label: Compare fairly
steps.text: Compare the same summary across groups (mean with mean, count with count); do not compare a group mean with a group total. (Notes section 3.3)

blocks.takeaway: One summary value per nonempty group. (Notes sections 3.1-3.2)
